notes: Build/render commands were rerun after final normal and bevel cleanup.
No git push, PBR, UV, animation, or Web command was run.

measurement_method.actual: evaluated mesh vertices projected through final Blender review cameras

registration.method: single per-view helmet bbox height and center, no per-feature fit

observed: Eye inner and outer loops had unequal vertex counts, producing broken C-shaped fragments.
Rear ridge and vent geometry was occluded by the retained rear shell.
The old crown cap still produced a circular top highlight/opening artifact.
Side cheek overlay polygons intersected into blocky lower-shell fragments.
changes: Replaced eye loops with equal-count measured rounded slots.
Raised ridge, vent, and rear-layer projection offsets.
Added an apex bridge and replaced side overlay blocks with measured diagonal grooves.

iterations.scope: eye topology and rear/crown visibility correction
observed: Ear disks reached the measured large concentric scale.
Back ridge, vents, and layer seams became readable.
Eyes were topologically complete but mostly buried by the faceplate surface.
Apex bridge was over-thick.
changes: Changed eye housing to a full black backing patch with a cyan lens layer.
Added vertical boundary fade to faceplate relief.
Reduced apex bridge size and darkened ridge material.

iterations.scope: complete eye slit and reduced crown bridge
observed: Both cyan eye slits were complete and horizontal.
The slits projected too far and the old Temple boundaries visually cut their outer ends.
A circular crown depression remained around the closed bridge.
changes: Tested raising the measured faceplate ahead of Temple and seating the eye layers closer.
Tested a same-red crown center cover under a narrower black cap.

iterations.scope: raised faceplate and red crown cover test
observed: Raising the entire faceplate exposed the measured boundary but introduced strong surface folds.
The flat red crown cover read as a square plaque rather than a shell repair.
Eye pieces were still split by varying surface normals.
changes: Rejected global faceplate lift and restored shallow projection.
Moved Temple vertices rearward instead of moving the faceplate.
Tested a shared fixed-forward eye plane and projected elliptical crown cover.

iterations.scope: rear-seated Temple and fixed eye plane
observed: Temple no longer occluded the measured gold boundary.
Eye slits were complete but visibly detached in top view.
The elliptical crown cover created a new ring highlight.
Smooth side-wall normals produced a false sawtooth highlight on the faceplate edge.
changes: Returned eyes to the same analytic faceplate relief with controlled 4.5/6 mm layer offsets.
Split projected skin normals from explicit thickness walls.
Removed the red cover and retained the closed black crown cap.

iterations.scope: surface-following eyes and split boundary normals
observed: Eye slits were complete, surface-following, and inside the faceplate in front view.
The faceplate/CrownFront surfaces remained nearly coplanar at the upper edge, causing a local ragged intersection.
changes: Seated CrownFront 4 mm rearward while leaving the v3 master silhouette and pivot unchanged.

observed: Measured V boundary and black bezel are readable without a coplanar intersection.
Eyes, ear disks, diagonal U frame, segmented crown/rear ridge, vents, and rear layers are all readable in their required views.
The crown center is closed by a black ridge cap; no through-opening is visible.
Faceplate brow, nose, mouth recess, and chin relief produce continuous front-three-quarter highlights.
changes: No further geometry change; candidate frozen for final measured validation and export.

visual_self_check_D4.observation: Brow shelf, central nose ridge, mouth recess, and forward chin produce separated highlights.
Both horizontal cyan lenses are enclosed by black housings and remain inside the measured gold faceplate bbox.
Black trim is visible at the top notch, temples, cheek rails, and lower edge.
Continuous diagonal rails connect the cheeks to the lower U; no horizontal louver bands are used for the front jaw.
Both side views show a large red flange, black outer ring, inset center disc, and vertical cyan emitter.
Back view shows eight dark ridge modules, paired horizontal vents, and mirrored upper/lower layer seams.
A solid CrownSpine_Cap closes the apex; the faceplate surface has continuous highlight flow without the v3 upper wrinkles.

known_issues: This is a complete feature graybox, not production retopology; small side/rear fasteners and micro-panels from the concept sheet remain simplified.
The source turnaround is internally inconsistent across views; front faceplate closure and side ear scale take priority over exact minor side-panel seams.
The solid apex cap remains intentionally readable as a raised service module so the former top through-opening cannot recur.
No PBR texture set, UV unwrap, rig, assembly animation, or Web integration is included.
